name: PublisherKits NewsDesk Manager
author: PublisherKits

sections.description:
NewsDesk Manager is an editorial inbox for news and trade publishers. It collects the press releases, newsroom feeds and official announcements your site may republish, scores each one against your audience and interests, and gives your editor one ranked queue to work through. Nothing is ever published on its own: the editor decides, and NewsDesk prepares a WordPress draft.

Sources you are allowed to use

  • RSS and newsroom feeds: press release wires, company newsrooms, official bodies, trade associations and partner feeds.
  • Email: a dedicated mailbox read over IMAP. Mail from a new sender waits in Needs attention until an editor approves the sender.
  • Team forwards: list the addresses your journalists forward press releases from. NewsDesk unwraps each forward (Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail or an attached message), uses the original sender, date and text, and credits the draft to the journalist.
  • Every source needs a recorded republish confirmation before anything is fetched.

Reuse rights on every item

Every candidate is graded Direct reuse, Reuse with credit, Background only or Off limits, with the reasons shown. The grade decides what a draft may contain: a Background only item never has its text copied, and an Off limits item cannot be drafted. Embargoed items are held until their release time. Copies of the same release sent to several addresses are folded into one.

A ranked review queue

Items are scored on topic match, audience fit, your site’s past engagement, freshness and source trust, with the breakdown one click away. Editors create a draft, dismiss or snooze, and every decision is recorded on your site with its reason, as a history of what your desk picked.

Drafts ready to edit

Create draft makes a WordPress draft with the source text, the credit, a link to the original and provenance details. Summary-only feed items are read in full from the source’s own website (robots.txt respected). Images that came with an item are listed with their clearance, and added to the Media Library only when an editor chooses one. A House Style tab holds your site’s style rules, shown beside every draft.

AI optional

NewsDesk works with no AI at all: scoring falls back to rules and says so. On WordPress 7.0 or later, with an AI provider configured at Settings > Connectors, you can switch on “Use AI judgement” in NewsDesk Settings (off by default) and NewsDesk uses the WordPress AI Client to judge audience fit and suggest a reuse grade. NewsDesk stores no AI key of its own.

PublisherKits Site Profile

If your site has a PublisherKits Site Profile, NewsDesk reads your topics, audience and exclusions from it. Without one, describe your interests on NewsDesk’s own Interests tab.

NewsDesk Manager Pro is a separate paid version that adds AI drafting to your house style with every quote and figure checked against the source, combining several items into one story, several mailboxes and AI sorting of new senders. Everything described above is in this free plugin and is not time-limited.

External services

NewsDesk contacts the services below only as described. It never sends your readers’ or subscribers’ data anywhere.

1. News feeds you register

The RSS or newsroom feeds you add, fetched through the WordPress HTTP API on the schedule set in Settings, only after you complete each source’s recorded republish confirmation. Each feed is governed by its publisher’s terms.

2. Your intake mailbox (optional)

Only if you connect one. NewsDesk logs in to the IMAP server you enter (encrypted connection, certificate checked) on the fetch schedule, on Fetch now and on Test connection, sending only the username and password, to that server only. It reads message headers and text and changes nothing in the mailbox. The password is stored encrypted with a key from your wp-config.php secret keys. Links in messages are never opened, and images in messages are never previewed.

3. Full articles and images from the source’s own website

When a feed item has only a summary, NewsDesk requests that one page from the address the feed gave, only on the source’s own website, after checking its robots.txt, identifying itself as PublisherKits-NewsDesk with your site address. For GOV.UK items it uses the public GOV.UK Content API (https://www.gov.uk/api/content/…). Terms: https://www.gov.uk/help/terms-conditions. This can be switched off per source. Images are downloaded only when an editor clicks “Use this image”, from the address the source published (an image an email links to, from the address in the email; an email attachment, from your own mailbox). Previews of feed images, in the draft and in Show original, load in your browser from the source’s website without a referrer; images an email links to are never previewed.

4. Your AI provider, via the WordPress AI Client (optional)

On WordPress 7.0 or later with a provider configured at Settings > Connectors, NewsDesk asks the WordPress AI Client to send each item being scored to that provider: its title and the first 800 characters of its text, with your interests and their importance, audience description and exclusions. The answer is a fit judgement and a suggested reuse grade. Nothing is sent unless an administrator ticks “Use AI judgement” in NewsDesk Settings (off by default); then it happens once per scored item. Test AI sends one tiny request when clicked. NewsDesk stores no AI key; removing the provider stops all calls. With the PublisherKits Content Classifier plugin active, topic sorting sends the title and first 1,500 characters to that plugin’s provider under its own disclosures; otherwise sorting runs on your server. NewsDesk Manager Pro (not part of this plugin) also sends: when an editor clicks Create draft (Settings > Create draft, on by default) or the AI draft button, the item (title, source, date, link, up to 16,000 characters, or 24,000 for an article or combined story) with your house style, then the draft and source for a meaning check, up to 5,000 characters of the draft with your audience for an image caption, and for emailed releases up to 6,000 characters to name the organisation to credit; and only if an administrator switches on Settings > New senders (off by default), up to 3 emails (1,500 characters each) and 15 subjects per sender awaiting approval.

The data is governed by your provider’s terms. For Anthropic, the default model: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

5. PublisherKits Support Service (optional help assistant)

The Help button opens a support assistant backed by the PublisherKits support service at https://bwtlsupport.com/ (Black and White Trading Ltd). Nothing is sent until an administrator opens it and accepts its privacy notice. With an AI provider configured on your site, the assistant tries that provider first: your question goes to your provider, and the service is asked only for documentation matched to your installed version (no question or chat text is sent to it). If that local answer fails and your site is authorised to use the service, the assistant automatically falls back to the service, and your question and recent chat history are then sent to it as well. Without an AI provider, the service answers within a monthly allowance.

Sent with each request: your site address (to authorise it and apply the fair-use limit; a derived value is kept against a monthly counter for two months), plugin versions, the admin screen, a short list of non-sensitive counts (sources, channels, whether the AI judge is on and its model preference), support tier and question category, and the question and chat history (used to answer, not retained). The versions, diagnostics and response timings are kept only as aggregated daily counts. Press releases, drafts, passwords and keys are never sent. Only if you click “Send to support” are the transcript, diagnostics and the email you give kept so a person can reply.

Terms: https://publisherkits.com/terms/ Privacy: https://publisherkits.com/privacy-policy/

6. Freemius (licensing and optional usage data)

The Freemius SDK manages licences and updates for the paid version. On activation it asks whether you want to share basic site data (site address, WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, admin email) with Freemius. Nothing is sent unless you opt in, and you can opt out from the plugin’s Account page.

Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/ Privacy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin from Plugins > Add New, or upload the zip.
  2. Open PublisherKits > NewsDesk.
  3. On the Sources tab, add a feed and complete its republish confirmation, or connect an intake mailbox.
  4. Set your interests on the Interests tab (or Topic Priorities, with a Site Profile) and your style on the House Style tab.
  5. Click Fetch now, or wait for the scheduled fetch. New items appear on the Queue tab.
sections.faq:
Does NewsDesk publish anything automatically?

No. It only creates drafts when an editor asks. Publishing is always a person’s decision.

Do I need an AI provider?

No. Without one, scoring runs on rules and the screens say so. With WordPress 7.0 or later and a provider configured at Settings > Connectors, you can switch on “Use AI judgement” in NewsDesk Settings to add an AI judgement of audience fit. It is off until you do.

Will it change my mailbox?

No. NewsDesk reads mail without deleting, moving or marking it as read. Links in messages are never opened. Images in a message are never previewed (that would tell the sender it was opened): one is fetched only when an editor clicks “Use this image”.

Which mail services work?

Any mailbox reachable over IMAP with a password, including Google Workspace with an app password. Microsoft 365 does not allow password sign-in: forward its mail to a mailbox on your web host.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

By default your settings, sources, confirmations and decisions are kept, so a reinstall picks up where you left off. Tick “Delete all plugin data when uninstalling” in Settings to remove them.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0 – 2026-11-05

  • New: team forwarding. On the Sources tab, list the addresses your journalists forward press releases from, each against a WordPress user. Their forwards are unwrapped (Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail forwards, forwards of forwards, or a message attached whole) and use the original sender, date, subject and text; who forwarded it and their note are shown, and the draft is credited to them. A forward goes straight into the queue; the original sender is listed in Needs attention to approve or block. Trust comes from the team member’s address passing the mail server’s DMARC check; anything else is held.
  • New: “This publisher’s other websites” on the source form, so items linking to a publisher’s sister sites keep the source’s grade and their full text can be read there.
  • Changed (privacy): an image an email only links to is no longer previewed in the draft (that would tell the sender the email was opened). It is listed with the website it is on and fetched only when an editor clicks “Use this image”. Tracking pixels are not listed. “Show original” loads feed images without a referrer.
  • Fixed: a press release whose cover note offers an interview was treated as an interview offer and never drafted; a pitch offering to write a piece was drafted as if it were the article.
  • Fixed: embargo times further down a pitch, or written as “08:00am Thursday 5th Nov”, were missed or not read.
  • Fixed: forwarded releases were shown and credited as coming from your own intake mailbox; they now name the original sender. A forwarded release is no longer listed twice, and a release sent both direct and forwarded is taken once.
  • Fixed: ticking “Use AI judgement” now re-scores items already scored by the rules alone, and an item whose AI request failed is tried again.
  • Fixed: the score breakdown said “no AI provider” whenever the AI had not judged an item; it now gives the real reason. Strict model mode with the Default model refused every answer from a provider other than Anthropic.
  • Fixed: wording – the queue help no longer says NewsDesk learns from your reasons (they are recorded as a history), mailbox rows say “Edit mailbox”, and the stale-drafts heading says what it lists.
  • Fixed: uninstall with “Delete all plugin data” now removes every NewsDesk setting, and deactivating or uninstalling removes pending background jobs.

1.1.0 – 2026-10-24

  • Changed: AI judgement is now an explicit choice. With an AI provider configured at Settings > Connectors, NewsDesk sends nothing to it until you tick “Use AI judgement” in NewsDesk Settings (off by default). The setting says exactly what each request contains. If you used AI judgement before, tick the box once to keep it.
  • Fixed: the Help assistant’s privacy notice, the Support settings and this readme now say that when your site’s own AI cannot answer and the site is authorised for the PublisherKits support service, the assistant falls back to that service and sends it your question and recent chat history.
  • Fixed: on the PublisherKits Site Profile, tick-box questions that sit inside another question (such as which sources you have, or reader seniority) now save; previously those answers were lost on save.
  • Improved: settings forms read only their own fields, never the whole request, and the Support settings no longer strip a character from saved values.

1.0.1 – 2026-10-15

  • Updated Freemius SDK to the latest version.

1.0.0 – 2026-10-01

  • First public release: feed and mailbox intake with recorded republish confirmations, reuse grades, the ranked review queue, editing drafts, House Style and optional AI judgement.

upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Adds team forwarding of press releases, stops email images being previewed, and fixes interview-offer and embargo detection.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: AI judgement is now off until you tick "Use AI judgement" in NewsDesk Settings. If you used AI scoring before, tick it once to keep it. Also fixes saving of tick-box questions on the Site Profile.

screenshots.caption: The Review Queue: every item scored against your Site Profile and graded for reuse, best fit first.
Click a score to see why: each part of the score and the topics the item matched.
Sources: every feed carries a recorded republish confirmation (who, when and the exact URL) before anything is fetched.
Settings: AI judgement stays off until you tick it, and the setting says exactly what each request contains.
House Style: the editorial rules shown beside every draft NewsDesk creates.
